_partNote: Most classes here are substances rather than machines, so each tile draws the characteristic physical form the material takes when you can hold it: a loose heap of broken ore, a precise sintered magnet block, a stacked pyramid of cast ingots, a long cone-ended crystal boule, a honeycomb-faced catalyst puck, a short column of ceramic fuel pellets, and a strapped cube of crushed scrap. Nothing is poured, immersed or in a vessel, and the three small solids are held apart by proportion — a wide flat slab, a squat grid-faced cylinder, and a narrow stack of discs.

partPrompts.1: A loose heap of coarse angular ore lumps piled on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: about a dozen fist-sized broken rocks with flat fractured faces and sharp edges, mounded into a low pile wider than it is tall, with a few smaller chips lying around the base. Raw broken rock, nothing manufactured; no container, no sack, no machine, no powder.
partPrompts.2: A single sintered magnet block resting on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a precise rectangular slab with crisp square corners and a fine chamfer running around its top edges, about twice as long as it is wide and a third as thick, its faces smooth and evenly plated. Well off to one side and clearly smaller, a curved arc-segment magnet, a rectangular tile bowed into a shallow curve. Two precise machined solids with a clear gap between them; no poles marked, no field lines, no iron filings, no motor.
partPrompts.3: A stack of cast metal ingots, seen three-quarter: six identical bars of trapezoidal cross-section, wider at the base than the top, stacked three then two then one into a neat pyramid about twice as wide as it is tall, each bar's blunt end face clearly visible at the near side. Solid cast bars with softly rounded edges. No wire, no coil, no sheet, no crucible, no machine.
partPrompts.4: A single-crystal boule lying horizontally on two small support blocks, seen three-quarter: a long smooth round cylinder about four times as long as it is thick, drawn down to a blunt cone at one end, with a flat facet ground along its whole length so a straight edge runs down its side. One plain solid cylinder; no wafers, no discs, no grid of squares, no saw, no machine.
partPrompts.5: A round honeycomb catalyst monolith standing on end, seen three-quarter: a short thick cylinder about as tall as it is wide, its whole top face filled with a regular coarse grid of open square channels running straight through the block, a narrow chamfer around the rim and plain smooth sides. Coarse channels, not a fine mesh. One block on its own; no canister, no steel shell, no pipes, no exhaust, no vehicle.
partPrompts.6: A short stack of four ceramic fuel pellets standing on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: identical squat cylinders each about as tall as it is wide, set one on top of another into a small narrow column with the seams between them clearly visible, the top pellet showing a shallow dish in its end face and a small chamfer around its rim. Small precise ceramic cylinders and nothing else; no tube, no cladding, no rod, no bundle, no machine.
partPrompts.7: A single baled cube of crushed scrap sitting on a flat surface, seen three-quarter: a roughly cubic compressed block whose faces are made of flattened folded fragments jammed together, so the surface reads as irregular and lumpy rather than smooth, with two flat binding straps running around it. One dense cube; no loose heap, no powder, no bin, no conveyor, no machine.
